classification.difficultyReason: Apply vertical shifts to two logarithmic base graphs, coordinating three curves per sketch and identifying their common asymptote and distinct intercepts.

content.prompt: Use shifting to sketch each set of graphs on one set of axes, clearly indicating the asymptote and the intercepts with the axes.

answer.short:
All three have vertical asymptote $x=0$ and no $y$-intercept. Their $x$-intercepts, in the given order, are $(1,0)$, $(\tfrac12,0)$ and $(2,0)$.

Shift $y=\log_2 x$ up 1 unit and down 1 unit.
answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\log_2 x$ through $(\tfrac12,-1)$, $(1,0)$, $(2,1)$ and $(4,2)$.

Shift this curve up 1 unit for $y=\log_2 x+1$, giving points $(\tfrac12,0)$, $(1,1)$, $(2,2)$ and $(4,3)$.

Shift the original curve down 1 unit for $y=\log_2 x-1$, giving points $(\tfrac12,-2)$, $(1,-1)$, $(2,0)$ and $(4,1)$.

All three approach the vertical asymptote $x=0$. Since their domain is $x>0$, none intersects the $y$-axis. Label the $x$-intercepts $(\tfrac12,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(2,0)$ on the shared axes.

spec.description: Three increasing logarithmic curves on shared axes. Separate line-style legend identifies each equation; the y-axis is the common vertical asymptote. No grid is supplied or required.
spec.mathematics: Vertical translations of log base 2 by 0, +1 and -1; x-intercepts 1, 1/2 and 2 respectively; no y-intercepts.

answer.short:
All three have vertical asymptote $x=0$ and no $y$-intercept. Their $x$-intercepts, in the given order, are $(1,0)$, $(4,0)$ and $(\tfrac14,0)$.

Shift $y=-\log_2 x$ up 2 units and down 2 units.
answer.worked:
Sketch $y=-\log_2 x$ through $(\tfrac14,2)$, $(\tfrac12,1)$, $(1,0)$, $(2,-1)$ and $(4,-2)$.

Shift this curve up 2 units for $y=2-\log_2 x$, giving points $(\tfrac14,4)$, $(\tfrac12,3)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$ and $(4,0)$.

Shift the original curve down 2 units for $y=-2-\log_2 x$, giving points $(\tfrac14,0)$, $(\tfrac12,-1)$, $(1,-2)$, $(2,-3)$ and $(4,-4)$.

All three approach the vertical asymptote $x=0$. Since their domain is $x>0$, none intersects the $y$-axis. Label the $x$-intercepts $(\tfrac14,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(4,0)$ on the shared axes.

spec.description: Three decreasing logarithmic curves on shared axes, with a separate line-style legend and labelled intercept ticks. The y-axis is the common vertical asymptote. No grid is supplied or required.
spec.mathematics: Vertical translations of negative log base 2 by 0, +2 and -2; x-intercepts 1, 4 and 1/4 respectively; no y-intercepts.
